title: The enormous turnip.
lines: Once upon a time there was a grandpa who had a little vegetable garden.
In spring he planted all sorts of seeds.
Carrot seeds, lettuce seeds and one little turnip seed.
Grow well, little turnip, said Grandpa, and he watered it.
The sun shone, it rained a little, and the turnip grew.
It became the biggest turnip in the whole world.
In autumn Grandpa said: Now I'm going to pull my turnip out of the ground.
He took hold of the leaves and he pulled.
Grandma held on to Grandpa, and Grandpa held on to the turnip.
The girl held on to Grandma, Grandma held on to Grandpa, Grandpa held on to the turnip.
The dog held on to the girl, the girl held on to Grandma, Grandma held on to Grandpa, Grandpa held on to the turnip.
The cat held on to the dog, the dog held on to the girl, the girl held on to Grandma, Grandma held on to Grandpa, and Grandpa held on to the turnip.
But the turnip still stayed put.
Then the cat called the very smallest animal in the garden.
Can such a little mouse really help?
The mouse held on to the cat, the cat held on to the dog, the dog held on to the girl, the girl held on to Grandma, Grandma held on to Grandpa, Grandpa held on to the turnip.
The turnip shot out of the ground!
And everyone fell backwards on their bottoms.
Grandpa, Grandma, the girl, the dog, the cat and the mouse all lay in the grass, laughing so hard.
And even the very smallest mouse can make a difference.
That evening Grandma made a big pot of turnip soup.
The mouse got the first bowl.
